hints: Focus on electrons first, not atoms. This is a redox change where chromium is reduced and iron is oxidised.
Each chromium in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ goes from +6 to +3, so two chromiums gain 6 electrons in total while each $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ loses only 1 electron.
Balance the electrons gained and lost to find how many $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions are needed for one dichromate ion, then check charge balance.
walkthrough:
**Write the two half-equations**

Think of this as two jobs happening at once. Chromium is gaining electrons (reduction) and iron is losing electrons (oxidation).

Reduction: $$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Oxidation: $$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^-$$

**Balance the electrons**

One dichromate ion needs 6 electrons to make 2 $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions. This is because each Cr goes from +6 to +3, a gain of 3 electrons, and there are 2 Cr atoms.

$$2 \times 3e^- = 6e^- \text{ gained}$$

**Scale up the iron half-equation**

Each $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ gives away only 1 electron. To supply the 6 electrons needed, we need 6 $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions.

$$6(\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^-)$$

**Combine and check**

Add the half-equations together and cancel the electrons to get the full ionic equation.

$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 6\text{Fe}^{2+} + 14\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 6\text{Fe}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Quick charge check: left side is $-2 + 12 + 14 = +24$, right side is $+6 + 18 = +24$. Balanced, so this is the correct equation.

options.A: Incorrect. With only 1 $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, only 1 electron is supplied but dichromate needs 6 electrons. Charge is also unbalanced (+13 on left, +9 on right).
options.B: Incorrect. With 2 $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, only 2 electrons are supplied, not the 6 needed for $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. Students sometimes guess 2 because there are 2 Cr atoms.
options.C: Incorrect. With 3 $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, only 3 electrons are supplied. This comes from forgetting there are 2 Cr atoms, each needing 3 electrons, so 6 in total, not 3.
options.D: Correct. 6 $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions each lose 1 electron to give the 6 electrons required to reduce $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. Atoms and charge (+24 both sides) are fully balanced.
